newsitem.title: UK: Australian scientists find figerprints reveal everything.
newsitem.headline: Australian scientists find figerprints reveal everything.

text.p: Australian scientists said on Wednesday they had found another reason for criminals to wear gloves -- a person's fingerprint also carries some of their DNA.

DNA "fingerprints" have been taken from hair, blood and semen, but Roland van Oorschot and Maxwell Jones of the Victoria Forensic Science Centre said they had also found the genetic material in fingerprints.

"We show that an individual's genetic profile can now also be generated from swabs taken from objects touched by hands, providing a new tool for crime scene investigations," they wrote in a letter to the science journal Nature.
They first tested to see if they could get DNA when they swabbed the palms of volunteers. They succeeded.
They then tested objects regularly handled by the volunteers. "Objects included leather briefcase handles, a personal locker handle and telephone handsets," they wrote.
"One of the telephone handsets also clearly displayed the genetic profile of a known secondary (minor) user," they added.

"Furthermore, a number of pre-cleaned objects held for a relatively short period of time (15 minutes), including a plastic knife handle, a mug, a glass, as well as new vinyl gloves worn for 20 to 90 minutes, gave the genetic profile of the holder or wearer."
DNA was even transferred after a handshake, they said.
They said police had started using the technique.
"Our methods have already been used at our laboratory to provide evidence in attempted murder, rape, armed robbery, extortion and drug-trafficking cases," Oorschot and Jones wrote.
